question: Will the U.S. Trustee's official committee of unsecured creditors in The Children's Place Chapter 11 case have seven or more members as of November 27, 2026?

calls.reasoning: No committee appointed as of the Nov 10 interim DIP order and Nov 13 case summaries. Region 3 typically appoints committees in large retail cases within ~10-14 days (Rite Aid 2025: 11 days; BBBY 2023: 12 days), so P(notice filed by ~Nov 25, 17 days post-petition) ~0.85. DNJ UST forms say the committee 'ordinarily' consists of holders of the 7 largest willing claims, and big NJ retail cases have gotten 7-9 (Rite Aid 2025: 9). But this is a smaller liquidation with $94M top-30 trade debt concentrated in Asian suppliers, where 5-member committees are common; landlords could push it up. P(>=7 | appointed) ~0.45. No market found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold; I did not separately check Kalshi/bookmakers).
calls.dossier:
- Petition filed Nov 8, 2026 (D.N.J., Judge Meisel, Case 26-22682); 13 debtors; $881.3M liabilities; fleetwide store-closing sales began Nov 6; dual-track sale of brands (bid deadline Dec 9, sale hearing Dec 15). [chapter11cases.com, Nov 13 2026; bondoro]
- No official UCC appointed as of the interim DIP order (Nov 10) or as of case summaries published Nov 13, 2026; docket through No. 110 (Nov 12) shows no notice of appointment. [chapter11cases.com; bondoro; question background]
- Top-30 unsecured list: $93.9M trade, $76.2M of it owed to 21 Asian creditors (sourcing/manufacturing); Hansae $15.4M largest. [bankruptcydata.com; WWD/Sourcing Journal]
- Retail debtor with roughly 500 stores, so landlords are potential committee candidates as well as vendors.
- D.N.J. U.S. Trustee solicitation forms: the committee 'ordinarily consists of the persons, willing to serve, who hold the seven (7) largest unsecured claims' (boilerplate). [justice.gov/ust/media/1383341]
- Region 3 DNJ comparables: Rite Aid 2025, filed ~May 5, 9-member committee appointed May 16, 2025 (Law360). Bed Bath & Beyond, filed Apr 23, 2023, committee appointed May 5, 2023 (12 days; size not confirmed in this research). Rite Aid 2023 reportedly also had a large committee.
- Typical Region 3 lag from petition to appointment in large retail cases: about 10-14 days. Cutoff: filing date on or before Nov 27; courts closed Nov 26 (Thanksgiving), so effectively Nov 25 = day 17 post-petition.
- Smaller or liquidating retail cases often get 3-5 member committees; committees dominated by foreign (Asian) vendors sometimes have fewer willing members, though Asian suppliers have served on recent US retail committees.
- Resolves off the most recent UST notice of appointment on the Omni docket (clientid=3814) or PACER, counting named members only (not professionals). No notice by the cutoff = NO.
- Event window: Nov 8 petition -> Nov 27, 2026 filing-date cutoff; as of Nov 16, about 42% of the 19-day window has elapsed (~9 days remain, ~7 business days).
- Searched but not found: any docket entry, news item or formation-meeting notice after Nov 13; the Omni docket and Law360 returned 403 errors; no prediction market found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold).
calls.reference_class: Official unsecured creditor committees appointed by U.S. Trustee Region 3 (D.N.J./D. Del.) in mid-to-large retail chapter 11 liquidation/sale cases, 2023-2026

calls.reasoning: No committee had been appointed as of docket No. 110 (Nov 12). The D.N.J. U.S. Trustee's best-efforts 14-day target and recent large New Jersey retail cases (11-12 days) give about 0.85 that a notice is filed by the effective Nov 25 cutoff. If one is appointed, seven or more is a bit below a coin flip: the solicitation form says 'seven largest' and recent comparables got 7 and 9, but this is a liquidation with a modest trade pool concentrated in Asian manufacturers who may decline, the landlords Simon and Brookfield may be conflicted as investors in a bidder, and a recent New Jersey case got 5. 0.85 x ~0.48 is about 0.41.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts: no committee by Nov 12, an effective Nov 25 cutoff, the 'seven largest' solicitation language, and comparable sizes of 7 and 9 (larger cases) versus 5 (Del Monte). The timing estimates (0.83-0.88) rest on the U.S. Trustee's 14-day best-efforts target. I accept about 0.85. The size question is a judgment call. I weight the liquidation posture, the concentrated foreign vendor pool and the possible Simon/Brookfield conflict slightly above the boilerplate 'seven' language, which gives about 0.48 conditional on appointment. Run 2's claim of a June 2026 committee in a same-numbered case conflicts with the Nov 8 petition date and is disregarded. I retrieved nothing new and had no web access.
